answer: Marginal-Clone Loss Mechanism. Each new agent passes a one-time inlet challenge: solve a unique, resource-heavy puzzle whose solution seeds its reputation key. The key must accumulate a quartz threshold of verified interactions before earning fees. An attacker cloning identities pays the full compute cost per clone, but clone revenue is capped by a shared ridge limit tied to the parent key, so each added clone earns less than its puzzle cost. Marginal clones are strictly negative-EV; profits come only from genuine distinct service.
